messages:
Kelly (People Ops): Heads-up — we're rolling out updated guidance for WFH stipends and relocations today. TL;DR: standard WFH stipend is $100/month (prorated on the first month), and any employee relocations need a tax-nexus + payroll intake before the move. Please read below and file the relocation form if you're moving. :wave:

Nina (Eng Manager): Quick Q — how does prorating work if someone starts mid-month or moves mid-month?

Kelly (People Ops): Good Q. Stipend is prorated by calendar days in the first month automatically. For moves mid-month, we prorate the stipend and update the payroll address effective the move date.

Dave (IC): If someone moves across state lines (e.g., CA -> NV) does that automatically create corporate nexus or just payroll withholding changes?

Omar (Finance): Short answer: moving an employee primarily creates payroll withholding and state unemployment tax obligations in the new state. Corporate tax/sales nexus is more nuanced and depends on business activity in that state. We'll flag any move that looks like it increases business presence for legal to review.

Kelly (People Ops): Action items: People Ops will kick off payroll update once we have the new address + move date. For any relocation package > $10,000 we need to evaluate tax treatment (reimbursement vs. taxable income) — receipts/accountable-plan preferred. @Omar can you confirm the guideline?

Omar (Finance): Confirmed. We generally treat direct reimbursements under an accountable plan as non-taxable if receipts are provided and expenses meet policy. Lump-sum relocation payments are typically taxable. I'll drop a short note in the #finance channel with the breakdown and the gross-up thresholds we use.

Nina (Eng Manager): What about international moves (US -> UK or EU)? Any immediate blockers we should know about?

Omar (Finance): Global moves require 2 things: (1) payroll vendor check (we may need to set up local payroll or use global payroll partner), and (2) tax/residency review (could create withholding and employer liabilities). Recommend filing the relocation request at least 60 days before the planned move so we can engage payroll and legal.

Kelly (People Ops): Filing link + quick checklist:

```
Relocation Request form: https://redwoodincorp.internal/forms/relocation
Checklist for submissions:
- new home address + effective move date
- relocation allowance breakdown (travel, shipping, temporary housing)
- receipts if claiming accountable reimbursement
- manager approval
- HR/People Ops contact for support
```

Kelly (People Ops): If you're doing a permanent move that changes your country/state of residence, expect benefits impacts (health plan, dependent coverage) and possible changes to 401(k) or pension rules. We will coordinate benefits enrollment changes.

Dave (IC): I'm planning a June 15th move from OR -> WA. I will file now. Any special WA notes?

Kelly (People Ops): Thanks @Dave — WA has different state withholding and next-quarter unemployment filings, but not a corporate nexus red flag by default for a single IC. We'll update payroll and benefits. Please include tentative move schedule + receipts for any reimbursed items.

Omar (Finance): Also tagging tax-bot for automatic checklist: @tax-bot please create payroll task and state-withholding change for Dave once the form is submitted.

tax-bot: automated: created payroll ticket #PR-2345, assigned to Payroll Ops. ETA: 3 business days to process address change. :white_check_mark:

Kelly (People Ops): Final note — if managers or ICs have questions about gross-up options or taxable treatment, escalate to @Omar. For any hires who request permanent remote relocation as a hiring condition, please loop People Ops before offer sign-off so we can vet tax and benefit impacts. :calendar: :rocket:

Dave (IC): Filing complete — submitted move date and estimated costs. Thanks! :thumbsup:
